title: Ali in the bed
hookLine: Ali sleeps in the Prophet's bed, and stays to return the Meccans' deposits (sirah)

cards: Night. Outside the house of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, young men from every clan are waiting with their swords, watching the door. Ibn Ishaq says they planned to strike when he came out.
Inside, the Prophet turns to his young cousin, Ali, and gives him a strange instruction. Lie down on my bed. Wrap yourself in my green cloak and sleep in it.
Nothing you dislike will happen to you. Today: Ali in the bed.

teach.b: So Ali lies down where the men outside expect their target to be. Through the night they see a shape under the Prophet's cloak, and they wait.

Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet went out among them, took a handful of dust, and scattered it over their heads, reciting from Ya Sin: and We have covered them so that they see not. He passed, and they didn't see him.
In the morning someone tells them he's gone. They look at the bed again, and it's Ali who gets up. But Ali's job isn't finished.
Ibn Ishaq says that people in Mecca who had something they feared for left it with the Prophet, because he was known for his honesty.
Tradition calls him al-Amin, the trustworthy.
When he left, Ibn Ishaq says, he told Ali to stay behind and return every one of those deposits to its owners. And Ali did.
For days, in a city that had just tried to kill his cousin, he went door to door handing back what belonged to them.
Then he set out for Yathrib himself. Some of the people who had left those deposits were the same people who wanted him dead.
And the Prophet's instruction about them, on the night he ran for his life, was about their property: make sure they get it back. Trust held, even toward them.

how: Muslims retell Ali's night in the Prophet's bed as part of the hijra story, and point to the returned deposits when they speak of amana, keeping what is entrusted to you.

o: the trustworthy, what Mecca called him
the generous one, a title for Mecca's merchants
the swift one, who left Mecca by night

games.q: Ali in the bed — tap the pairs.
p: waited at the door with swords

s: the men outside saw the Prophet leave
Ibn Ishaq says he scattered dust over them and passed, and they did not see him.
Ali left Mecca the same night
he stayed behind to return the deposits, then set out.
people who rejected his message trusted him with their valuables
Ibn Ishaq says Meccans who feared for their things left them with him, for his honesty.

games.q: you're the Prophet, leaving at night with killers at your door. people who want you gone have left valuables with you. what do you do?
o: have Ali stay and return them.
games.why: he told Ali to stay in Mecca and return every deposit to its owner, and Ali did, before setting out himself.

practice: Take a slow inventory of what you're holding that isn't yours: a borrowed book, a dish from someone's kitchen, money you owe, a favor promised, even somebody's secret, which is also held in trust.
Let each one come to mind without guilt, just as a list, and picture handing one of them back. If you pray, you can ask God to help you keep what's entrusted to you.

wordCard.voice: Al-Amin, the trustworthy: what Mecca called the Prophet, the reason people left their valuables with him even the night men waited outside his door with swords. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a trust; something left in your keeping.

carryVoice: Your line: trusts returned, even then. Ali's job wasn't glamorous: knock, hand it back, next door. That's today's lesson.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Ali sleeps in the Prophet's bed in his green cloak; the Prophet scatters dust and recites Ya Sin; Ali stays to return the deposits)
